answer:
Configure a transient, incompressible, laminar 2D simulation of flow past a cylinder using pimpleFoam at Re = 100 so that the Karman vortex street regime is naturally triggered.
Set the cylinder diameter D to 1 m, the inlet velocity U_infinity to 1 m/s, and the kinematic viscosity nu to 1e-2 m^2/s, giving Re = U_infinity * D / nu = 100.
Build a one-cell-thick mesh in the z-direction so the case behaves as a true 2D problem.
Define the frontAndBack patch in constant/polyMesh/boundary with type empty and use type empty for frontAndBack in both 0/U and 0/p.
Use a 2D O-grid blockMesh around the cylinder with a near-wall cell spacing of roughly 0.005 D to resolve the laminar boundary layer (no y+ target needed since the flow is laminar).
Size the computational domain to approximately 20 D in the cross-stream direction and 30 D downstream of the cylinder.
Assign inlet U as fixedValue uniform (1 0 0) and inlet p as zeroGradient.
Assign outlet U as zeroGradient and outlet p as fixedValue uniform 0.
Assign cylinderWall U as fixedValue uniform (0 0 0) and cylinderWall p as zeroGradient.
Initialize the internal fields of U to uniform (1 0 0) and p to uniform 0.
Use the laminar transport model (no turbulence modeling) since the flow is laminar at Re = 100.
Set the time step to approximately 5e-4 s to keep the Courant number Co below 1 in the near-wake region.
Run the simulation long enough to capture roughly 20 to 30 shedding cycles, i.e., a non-dimensional time t * U_infinity / D of about 200 to 400, equivalent to roughly 50 to 150 s of physical time.
Configure the run so that clean FFT / post-processing of the lift or velocity signal can be performed to extract the Strouhal number.
